abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>The poverty of disease resistance gene reservoirs limits the breeding of crops for durable resistance against evolutionary dynamic pathogens. <jats:italic>Zymoseptoria tritici</jats:italic> which causes Septoria tritici blotch (STB), represents one of the most genetically diverse and devastating wheat pathogens worldwide. No fully virulent <jats:italic>Z. tritici</jats:italic> isolates against synthetic wheats carrying the major resistant gene <jats:italic>Stb16q</jats:italic> have been identified. Here, we use comparative genomics, mutagenesis and complementation to identify <jats:italic>Stb16q</jats:italic>, which confers broad-spectrum resistance against <jats:italic>Z. tritici</jats:italic>. The <jats:italic>Stb16q</jats:italic> gene encodes a plasma membrane cysteine-rich receptor-like kinase that was recently introduced into cultivated wheat and which considerably slows penetration and intercellular growth of the pathogen.</jats:p>
title: A wheat cysteine-rich receptor-like kinase confers broad-spectrum resistance against Septoria tritici blotch
